To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
holes in web of coldformed steel joist can reduce the ultimate strength and distortional buckling is a dominant failure mode in beams with slotted holes.

the strength of the joists with web holes decreases with increasing hole depth, the distortional buckling modes are the dominant elastic buckling mode, and the use of a waterjet cutting process is an accurate and effective way to produce custom holes in joists.

the ultimate strength of cold formed steel joists with rectangular web holes is reduced by hole depth, local buckling of the strip above the hole can be a dominant failure mode, and the Direct Strength Method equations need to be modified for use with beams with web holes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effect of web openings on the strength of C-section joists, and we have shown that the presence of web openings significantly reduces the strength of joists with respect to their unperforated counterparts.
the effect of web hole depth on the behavior of cold formed steel beams.
the effect of rectangular web holes on the behavior of C section coldformed joists.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a hole depth of 0.75t for the 800S20033 cross section and 1.0t for the 1200S197 cross section should be avoided to prevent a reduction in ultimate strength.
the use of web holes in cold formed steel joists can be detrimental to the strength and stiffness of the member and should be avoided if possible.
the presence of holes reduces the ultimate strength and stiffness of the joist specimens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AISI DirectStrength Method equations for unstiffened webs are conservative for the cross section types and hole sizes evaluated in this study.
the use of web holes in cold formed steel members should be limited to those cases which are critical to the performance of the member.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hole depth has a significant impact on the strength of a cold formed steel joist with a hole.

the AISI DirectStrength Method is not accurate for predicting the strength of cold formed steel joists with holes and the current design provisions should be updated to account for the influence of holes.
the hole size and location should be carefully designed and the cross sections should be stiff enough to resist the local buckling.
